- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap upward revisions or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects; apply a lagged dampening factor to prevent immediate reversal.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model often underreacts; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment shift, especially in first 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is stronger in sentiment-neutral periods; if sentiment is flat (±0.1), forecast should be closer to recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early days (1–7) when sentiment is bullish; apply a 1–2% downward bias for first 7 days if sentiment > 0.5.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven support.
